"within thirty (30) calendar days of such expiry or termination, return to Sparkling all of Sparkling's data"

reasons: The inserted Section 17(d) supplies every preferred atomic element: 6-month assistance window, then-current rates, 30-day return running from expiry/termination (not from a request), machine-readable format, and post-return deletion with written certification.

"commonly used, machine-readable format" is the operative equivalent of the playbook's "standard machine-readable format"; the 30-day deadline is expressly stated, so the two failed precision checks are not borne out by the operative text.
The request condition attaches only to transition assistance (a service that must be requested to be scheduled) and does not qualify the mandatory data return, deletion, or certification.
Minimality is satisfied: a single concise insertion fills an absent obligation without rewriting Section 17(b) or the survival paragraph; "reasonable" is a modest qualifier, not an added exception.
Intent preserved: no defined terms disturbed, no contradiction with the existing customer-side return/certification duty in 17(b), and numbering (d) follows the existing scheme.
